title: VRL Logistics Ltd - 539118 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: VRL Logistics Q2 FY27 total income rose about 20% YoY to INR967 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 23.3%, with management guiding 21-22% sustainable.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue growth was driven by roughly 11% higher goods transport volume (976,000 to 1,079,000 tons) and 9% higher freight realisation per ton (INR8,079 to INR8,840). EBITDA rose 43% to INR226 crore with margin up 367 bps to 23.3%, and PAT nearly doubled to INR103 crore (10.7% margin). Net debt fell to INR337 crore from INR440 crore at March 2026, and a INR280 crore buyback at INR320 per share closed for tenders on 2 November 2026 with settlement due 9 November. Management flagged fuel cost volatility as the main risk and said freight rates would be cut in step with any fuel price reduction of about 5% or more.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR314 crore in H1 last year

financial_highlights.value: INR158 crore (Q1 INR76 crore, Q2 INR82 crore)

segments.name: Goods transport (B2B LTL)
segments.commentary: Volume up about 9.5-10% in H1 and expected to grow similarly in H2; FMCG and textile were the strongest commodities. Over 10 lakh customers, with paid and to-pay collection keeping receivable days at about 10-11.

segments.name: Contractual business
segments.commentary: Contractual customers make up about 17-18% of revenue and carry fuel escalation clauses; non-contractual rates are set at management's discretion.

segments.name: Branch network
segments.commentary: 51 branches added in Q2 and 67 in H1 (60+ opened in FY27 per the Q&A). New branches contributed about 2 percentage points of the roughly 10% H1 volume growth.

guidance_outlook: Tonnage growth of 9-10% expected in H2 FY27 and considered achievable for the medium term, up from the earlier 7-8% view.
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 21-22%, with management saying 23% plus is sustainable at current volumes and cost structure.
Revenue growth of at least 10-12% in the next year if realisation holds steady.
H2 FY27 capex of about INR150-160 crore; annual capex of at least INR250-300 crore going forward.
ROCE expected at least 30% this year after the buyback, versus about 25% last year.
Buyback settlement on 9 November 2026; equity reduction to be reflected in the nine-month results to 31 December 2026.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex of about INR158 crore went to commercial vehicles and land and buildings at Vijayawada, Nagpur, Lucknow and Raipur.
Fleet of 5,941 vehicles at end-H1; about 76% debt-free and about 11% fully depreciated.
Future fleet additions will shift to higher-capacity vehicles (25-30 tons) in fewer units, with total capacity growing roughly in line with tonnage.
Scrappage of older vehicles, running for about 1.5 years, is expected to be largely finished, so gross additions should rise.
Bangalore facility acquisition was underwritten at a 10-12 year payback; smaller property buys are need-based.
demand_pricing: Freight rates rose about 5% from 1 April and about 4% in mid-May, a cumulative 9% that drove the realisation gain.
Management said the rate increases did not hurt volumes; tonnage growth reached about 10% in H1 against an initial FY27 plan of about 8%.
October tonnage grew about 20% YoY; management said competitors could not book Ahmedabad-Surat textile loads during festival peak.
Claim ratio described as near zero versus 10-12% at other operators.
Fuel rule of thumb: every INR2 per litre change in fuel moves freight rates by about 1%. A 5% (about INR5) fuel cut implies about 2.5% realisation reduction, with margins held.
Bulk fuel buying is currently uneconomic: bulk at about INR120-125 versus about INR98-100 open market. Fuel cost per litre rose from about INR85 to INR97.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the margin and what EBITDA level should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 21-22% is sustainable, and later said 23% plus is achievable at current volumes and costs, with toll and overhead increases costing 1-1.5 points.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 9-10% volume growth continue into the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said 9-10% is achievable for H2 and the medium term, given market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: How will a fuel price cut affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rates would be cut only if fuel fell by 5% or more; on non-contract routes, VRL can retain prices where competition is limited. Margins would be held.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and capital allocation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 capex of INR150-160 crore, with the rest of cash used to reduce debt; longer term capex of at least INR250-300 crore a year, mainly vehicles and existing properties.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for employee wage increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is reviewing the increment process and will announce it later, with no timeline set; the hike is not yet decided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue growth outlook after the realisation gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Assuming no further price change, revenue growth of at least 10-12% for the next year, with volume at 9-10% plus a 1-2% realisation correction effect.

risks_watch: Fuel price direction: a sustained cut would force a freight rate reduction, and management said margin would hold only if fuel falls by about 5%.
Toll, loading/unloading and overhead inflation could cost about 1-1.5 margin points, which would push margin below the 23% level toward the 21-22% range.
Wage increment for employees is pending with no timeline; a Q3-style hike would add cost.
Realisation dependent on price discipline; competition on non-contractual and open-market routes could limit pass-through.
Execution of the H2 volume target (9-10%) and the branch expansion in North and East India, where presence is still limited.
Management said the buyback settlement is due 9 November 2026 and that ROCE would reach 30%+ this year; watch the Q3 numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume, margin and cash flow, with a strong focus on the service differentiation. Management was less specific on the fuel-linked pricing response and the timing of the employee pay review, and gave hedged answers on the medium-term margin.
key_quotes: This performance reflects an improvement in the quality of our earnings, with higher freight realizations, better cost absorption and stronger operating leverage contributing to our expanding margins.
Yes, around 21%-22% is a sustainable EBITDA margin even going forward.
For every INR2 change in the fuel rate, there is a 1% change in the freight rates.

Commercial vehicles and land/buildings at Vijayawada, Nagpur, Lucknow, Raipur (H1 FY27 capex INR158 cr); H2 FY27 capex INR150-160 cr

growth.why: Management guides tonnage growth of 9-10% for H2 FY27 and medium term and revenue growth of at least 10-12% next year if realisation holds, backed by 60+ branch openings in FY27, H2 capex of INR150-160 cr and a 5,941-vehicle fleet, plus a 9% cumulative freight rate hike, though no specific order book or utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management calls 21-22% sustainable and says 23%+ achievable at current volumes, but toll and overhead inflation could cost 1-1.5 points and fuel moves could squeeze margin; Q2 EBITDA margin was 23.3%, up 367 bps YoY.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 60+ branches opened in FY27 (67 in H1, 51 in Q2), H2 capex of INR150-160 crore goes to commercial vehicles and land/buildings, and future additions shift to 25-30 ton vehicles with capacity growing roughly in line with tonnage.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 9-10% tonnage growth for H2 FY27 and the medium term, up from 7-8%, after H1 growth of about 10% and October growth of about 20% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H2 FY27 capex of INR150-160 crore is guided and annual capex is raised to at least INR250-300 crore, with no utilisation figure given to size the need.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Tonnage growth guidance was raised to 9-10% from 7-8%, and H1 realisation rose about 9%, but the 21-22% margin and 10-12% revenue guide already sit below the H1 run-rate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: A sustained fuel cut would force freight rate cuts (about 2.5% realisation cut per 5% fuel fall), and toll/overhead inflation could cost 1-1.5 margin points, pulling margin toward 21-22%.

rows.label: Employee wage increment pending
rows.why: Management is reviewing the increment process with no timeline set, and a Q3-style hike would add cost against a 23.3% EBITDA margin.

rows.label: Fuel-linked freight rate cut
rows.why: Freight rates would fall only if fuel drops 5% or more (about INR5/litre, with fuel at about INR97/litre), implying about a 2.5% realisation cut with margins held.

rows.label: INR280 crore buyback settlement and ROCE rise
rows.why: Buyback at INR320 per share closes with settlement on 9 November 2026, and management expects ROCE of at least 30% this year versus about 25% last year.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume (9-10% guided), margin (21-23%) and cash flow, but hedged on fuel-linked pricing, the wage review timing and the medium-term margin; analysts pushed on margin sustainability and fuel pass-through.
